name: Andorra
rule: Andorra food-activities regulation Article 29 requires an origin health certificate for non-animal foods arriving from outside the EU. Articles 2 and 5 include imported and processed foods. This documentary requirement applies to the Japanese finished-tea product independently of the unresolved plant-health classification.
personalMailApplicability: The food import provision is general and contains no personal, small-quantity or postal exception; commercial sale to a consumer is not exempted.
authority: Andorra official legal portal, 2013 phytosanitary regulation and 2021 annex amendment
remainingQuestion: No certificate-free personal-post exception was established; do not use this destination under the store’s no-special-documents policy.
researchAttempts: Read the plant-product definitions and certificate annex in the official phytosanitary regulation.
Searched Andorran agriculture and customs guidance for tea and private postal imports; did not establish a finished-tea exception.
Read the full consolidated food-activities regulation, including scope, processed-food definition, Article 29 health-certificate requirement and the complete text for personal-use exemptions.
permitFreeReason: Article 29 of the consolidated food-activities regulation requires an origin health certificate for non-animal foods imported from a non-EU country. Its definitions include manufactured foods and its scope covers imported foods generally; no small personal-post exemption is stated. This requirement alone conflicts with the store’s no-certificates policy.

name: Albania
rule: Legal classification inference: Order 461 of 12 May 2025 replaced the certificate commodity annex under Order 113/2022. Annex IX Part B lists ex 090210/ex 090220 only as fresh, whole, uncut, unfermented green tea. Manufactured steamed/dried retail sencha is outside that description.
personalMailApplicability: The commodity-based certificate schedule governs imports generally, so this conclusion applies to personal postal tea and does not rely on a baggage allowance.
authority: Albanian Ministry of Agriculture; Official Gazette 97 of 4 June 2025, Order 461/2025, amending Order 113/2022
researchAttempts: Checked Law 105/2016 and the trade portal’s import-control description.

Searched for a tea-specific current rule and postal personal-use exemption without finding an authoritative determination.

Read Order 461/2025 effective 30 days after gazette publication; checked fresh-tea-only entry on printed page 14345 and the complete commodity certificate annex. This is current implementing law under Law 105/2016, not reliance on the future 2027 law.
permitFreeReason: The current implementing certificate schedule controls fresh tea leaves only; sealed steamed/dried sencha does not fit that regulated commodity. This rule applies to import consignments generally, including private postal orders. Ordinary customs declarations remain required.

name: Egypt
rule: Plant Quarantine Regulation 562/2019 Annex 10 item 11 exempts personal-use consignments of admissible items weighing no more than 50 kg from both import permits and phytosanitary certificates, excluding propagation material. CAPQ’s current commodity/origin database lists Japan (83), Tea Tree/Green Tea (955) with entry requirements, confirming this product/origin is admitted.
personalMailApplicability: Regulation 562 explicitly covers imported postal parcels, and Annex 10 item 11 covers personal-use consignments rather than only passenger baggage. The general database’s certificate/permit requirements are displaced by this specific personal-use exemption. Pests must still be absent and arrival inspection remains possible.

quantityLimit.scope: Personal-use consignment exemption from permit and phytosanitary certificate; applies only to items already allowed to be imported.

authority: Egypt Central Administration of Plant Quarantine: NPPO-published Regulation 562/2019 and current import-conditions database

permitFreeReason: The personal-consignment exemption waives both permit and phytosanitary certificate up to 50 kg for admitted non-propagating products. name: Gibraltar
rule: Current-law classification: Gibraltar implemented its EU customs-union arrangements on 15 July 2026. Sections 81 and 90 of the Treaty Act apply Union sanitary/phytosanitary entry formalities to third-country goods. Under the corresponding EU commodity rule, manufactured dried tea requires no phytosanitary certificate; the Swedish authority expressly confirms this for private orders.
personalMailApplicability: This applies to third-country goods generally, including postal purchases; it is not the passenger-baggage exception. Gibraltar Post requires the ordinary postal customs declaration. The personal-use organic-import exception also avoids an organic certificate of inspection for a recipient consuming the tea privately.
